# The wrapper compiles rewritten files from a directory of its own, and their
# names end up in the export data. Building the same package twice must still
# give the same archive: the go command can compile a package twice in one build
# (with PGO, once for each test binary that needs it), compile its importers
# against one copy and link the other, and the linker rejects two copies that
# differ.

env GOEXPERIMENT=simd
env LOOPVEC_TOOLEXEC_LOG=$WORK/log
env GOCACHE=$WORK/gocache1
exec go build -buildmode=archive -toolexec=$LOOPVEC_TOOLEXEC -o a1.a .
env GOCACHE=$WORK/gocache2
exec go build -buildmode=archive -toolexec=$LOOPVEC_TOOLEXEC -o a2.a .
grep -count=2 '^rewrote 1 loop\(s\) in example\.com/lib$' log
cmp a1.a a2.a

-- go.mod --
module example.com/lib

go 1.27.1
-- lib.go --
package lib

func Add(dst, a, b []float32) {
	for i := range dst {
		dst[i] = a[i] + b[i]
	}
}
